learning.title: A route path is a string, so the type checker cannot see it
learning.trigger: A test or fixture that passes type checking and fails on its first real call; or any change that moves a route path, a URL constant or a module specifier into a new module.
learning.symptom: A test module passes `deno check`, `pnpm fmt` and `pnpm lint`, and 404s on its first request. Nothing static is red, so on the first run the failure looks like a fixture or a server problem.
learning.cause: `deno check` types a string as a string. Every route path in every test is invisible to it, so a test can be type-clean and 404 on its first line. The type checker, the reviewer's diff read and the diff itself are all blind to this class by construction; only execution closes it.

rules.rule: A declared unexecuted state is not a formality to clear toward a merge. It is the only thing standing between a plausible path and a live one, so "I did not run it" stays legible in the record even when every other gate is green.
A head that moves under a tick gets announced. Ticks name a SHA, and a SHA that is no longer the head is a claim nobody re-made.
When relocating or copying test code, copy the constants from the module that owned them instead of retyping them from memory.

learning.evidence: Bakery #69 / PR 540. Moving a case out of `tests/helpers/ticket-admission/operations-integration.ts` into `tests/integration/read-the-tickets-linked-to-one-task_test.ts` retyped the source path as `/v1/external-ticket-sources`, which reads like the sibling of `/v1/external-tickets` and does not exist. The route table registers `/v1/ticket-sources` (`ticket-actions.ts:92,101`) and `ticket-routes.ts:25` guards it, so the preview call would have answered 404. `deno check`, `pnpm fmt` and `pnpm lint` were all clean at that commit; the defect was found by reading the route table, not by any gate, and fixed in `443ab7e96`. The class was named by qa-qa during review.
